text:
Braeden Bowman got a five-minute major and a game misconduct for elbowing Matthew Poitras in Boston on Nov. 2, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger reported, and the NHL decided against further discipline. Three nights later he scored a third-period equalizer in Detroit with what Granger called a "heck of a shot." That's a lot of story for an undrafted 23-year-old in his second NHL season.

On the ice, he's been useful and unlucky. He has 4 goals on 4.06 expected, exactly on schedule, but Vegas has scored 6.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, which has cost him points. Our talent range for his points rate (1.6 to 2.4 per 60) sits above where he is.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows a shooter who gets fed: 1.4 shots per 60 minutes off passes across the slot or from behind the net. He rarely carries the puck in himself (30% of entries) and isn't fast (10th percentile top speed). He came up through the Henderson Silver Knights. We project about 15 goals. Keeping the edge without crossing the line again is the real test.
headline: Bowman's week, both sides of it
